name: Social Affordance Reading and Mentalizing in Built Space
short_description: Mentalizing network (dmPFC, TPJ, temporal poles) continuously reads social affordances in built environments — inferring occupancy norms, behavioral scripts, social hierarchies; demands scale with social complexity of space
higher_order_principle: The mentalizing network (dmPFC, TPJ, temporal poles) continuously reads social affordances in built environments — inferring occupancy norms, behavioral scripts, social hierarchies, and interaction possibilities. This processing uses DMN mentalizing subsystem resources and its demands scale with the social complexity of the space.

neural_substrate.network: dmPFC + TPJ + temporal_poles (DMN dorsal medial subsystem)

scope_conditions: Applies when other people are present or their recent presence is inferable (traces, cues)
Mentalizing demands increase with social ambiguity — novel social situations require more dmPFC/TPJ
Cultural variation: social norms differ across cultures, modulating which cues are processed
Autism spectrum: reduced mentalizing network engagement changes relationship between social cues and behavioral decisions
moderators: familiarity (known people reduce mentalizing demand; strangers increase it)
social_anxiety (increases amygdala + mentalizing engagement, shifts toward avoidance)
architectural_legibility (clear social zoning reduces ambiguity, lowers mentalizing demand)

interactions.nature: Mentalizing uses DMN dorsal medial subsystem. Social affordance reading competes with self-referential processing for same neural resources.
Predictable social environments enable proactive social strategy; unpredictable social environments force reactive social processing.
T48 reads social affordances top-down (mentalizing). T49 processes social presence bottom-up (mirror/simulation). Both operate simultaneously.

key_references.citation: Lieberman, M. D. (2013). Social: Why Our Brains Are Wired to Connect. Crown.
